tools.change: METHOD DIFFERS FROM THE NATIONAL CHARTS. New Zealand's growth-chart fact sheet (health ministry, adapted from the UK college's material) predicts adult height from the CHILD'S OWN height centile on an adult-height prediction chart; it does not use a mid-parental formula. The tool uses a mid-parental formula with fixed constants and a fixed range that no New Zealand source read this session states. Change: a local paediatrician decides whether to keep it, re-source it, or replace it with the national chart's predictor.
tools.licence: Formula: a published paper (terms not read). National charts: copyright 2009 Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, adapted by the health ministry (needs permission).

tools.change: Unit confirmed: µg/L. The national referral guidance (2015) does not use a rate of change; it uses age-banded thresholds and a repeat test 6 to 12 weeks after an abnormal result. The tool warns "less than 90 days apart: read with caution", which fires on exactly that recommended repeat. bpacnz mentions a yearly rise as expert opinion only. Change: reword the caution; add the age-banded thresholds as a tool of their own (the guidance is CC BY 4.0).

tools.change: DOES NOT MATCH THE NATIONAL GUIDELINE. ACC's national concussion guidelines (updated January 2026) set six stages numbered 1 to 6 with minimum conditions: an earliest day for sport-specific training and a later earliest day for competition, counted from the injury. The tool has stages 0 to 5 with other names, no injury date and no minimum, so a doctor can record "full training and return to competition" with nothing recalling the national stand-down. Change: the stages, their names and the earliest days as the guideline states them, supplied and signed by a local sports physician.
tools.licence: ACC guideline: no licence statement in the document (needs ACC's permission to reproduce).

tools.change: KEEP OFF until fixed. Confirmed against bpacnz: laboratories report the albumin-to-creatinine ratio in mg/mmol and the categories are cut at 3 and 30 mg/mmol. The kit converts to mg/g and cuts at 30 and 300, so a value from 3.0 to about 3.3 mg/mmol is placed one category too low, and so is a value from just above 30 to about 33.9. Second fault: the tool's "referral to a nephrologist" flags are not New Zealand's; bpacnz lists different criteria (a higher albuminuria figure, a rule for diabetes, a kidney-failure risk figure, and a lower threshold for Māori and Pacific patients and for younger patients). Change: classify in mg/mmol; take the referral prompts from the local source or drop them; show it to general practice.
tools.licence: KDIGO grid: terms not read (unclear). bpacnz text: its own copyright (needs permission to reproduce).

tools.change: KEEP OFF until fixed: the same unit fault as the internal-medicine tool (limits at 3 and 30 mg/mmol are not the kit's converted limits).

kitGaps: A country cannot change WHO SEES a tool of the shared English set: the roles sit on the shared text (countries/_dil/en/araclar/*.ts, HamArac.roller). A pack can only switch a tool off (araclar.kapali) or reword it (araclar.degisen).
A country cannot add, drop or re-divide a role: all five English packs take the same 40 keys (EN_ROLLER), and lib/ulke/rolEslemesi.test.ts requires exactly forty.

A country cannot bring a tool of its own: every mechanism must be in the kit catalogue shared by all countries, and the tool texts and slots are the shared set's. EnAraclarGirdisi has no place for a country's own tools or own slots (beyond tools it closes).
New Zealand state-system tools (ACC, Work and Income, Pharmac) need an "nz" list in countries/yasak-araclar.json so that wall rule D7 keeps them out of every other country.
Thresholds are applied only in the kit's own unit after conversion (albumin-to-creatinine ratio in mg/g). A country whose published limits are in another unit (mg/mmol) cannot state them.
HbA1c has no unit choice (lab-izlem refuses values outside 3 to 20); LabOlcusu has no entry for it.
A pack's numbers (parametreler) are compared in the kit's unit, with nothing saying so: haemoglobin limits would have to be typed in g/dL in a country that reports g/L.
The options of a choice field are fixed in the kit (report categories, return-to-sport stages): a country cannot supply its own list.
Dose arithmetic has one unit (mg per kg): no micrograms, no units.
The citation shown under a result (kaynak) is fixed in the kit: a country cannot show its national source.
The patient file has no ethnicity and no deprivation quintile, both inputs of the national cardiovascular equations (the earlier audit, finding C8, already notes ethnicity).
A slot records what is missing and who supplies it, but not a licence status: there is no field to hold "permission asked / granted / refused" per tool per country.
